title: OR1-1 | Outcomes of Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty versus Medical Therapy in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension: A Real-World Analysis
full_text:
Background:
Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) can be managed with medical therapy alone or in combination with balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA). This study aimed to compare outcomes between these treatment strategies using real-world data.

Methods:
Using the TriNetX research network, we analyzed electronic medical records from 104 healthcare organizations. We identified CTEPH patients on anticoagulation who received either medical therapy alone (n=141) or medical therapy plus BPA (n=141). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics between groups. Primary outcomes included mortality, respiratory failure, and cardiopulmonary complications.

Results:
Results: Medical therapy plus BPA was associated with significantly lower mortality compared to medical therapy alone (7.8% vs 24.1%, OR 3.755, 95% CI 1.816-7.765, p<0.001). The BPA group also had lower rates of acute kidney injury (14.2% vs 27.0%, OR 2.232, 95% CI 1.223-4.075, p=0.008) and atrial fibrillation (14.9% vs 25.5%, OR 1.959, 95% CI 1.077-3.565, p=0.026). Heart failure rates were identical between groups (51.8% in both groups, OR 1.000, p=1.000). Other complications including respiratory failure (35.5% vs 39.7%, p=0.461), cardiogenic shock (7.1% vs 10.6%, p=0.295), cardiac arrest (7.1% vs 7.1%, p=1.000), and ventricular tachycardia (7.1% vs 7.1%, p=1.000) showed no significant differences between groups.

Conclusions:
In this real-world analysis, adding BPA to medical therapy significantly reduced mortality in CTEPH patients while maintaining a similar safety profile, supporting its use in eligible patients.
confex_title: OR1-1 Outcomes of Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty versus Medical Therapy in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension: A Real-World Analysis

title: OR1-2 | Comparing Outcomes of Endovascular Revascularization for Chronic Limb-threatening Ischemia in Medicare Advantage and Medicare Fee-for-service Beneficiaries
full_text:
Background


Enrollment in Medicare Advantage (MA), a private alternative to Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS), is projected to surpass FFS. The transportability of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) outcomes studies in the FFS population to MA is unknown. We compared endovascular revascularization outcomes for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) between MA and FFS beneficiaries.

Methods


Using Inpatient, Outpatient, Carrier, and MA Part C Encounter Data files, we identified patients undergoing lower extremity revascularization from 2018–2021. Socioeconomic status was assessed with the Distressed Communities Index. Baseline characteristics were compared with standardized mean difference. The primary outcome, a composite of major amputation and death, was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier methods and multivariable Cox regression, adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, revascularization modality, disease severity and other mediators.

Results


Among 453,228 patients (26.5% MA; 63.5% FFS), the MA cohort included more Black patients (21.4% vs. 15.7%), dual-enrolled patients (29.5% vs. 26.3%), and those from distressed communities (23.3% vs. 20.0%), but age, sex and comorbidity burden were comparable. At 4 years, the primary outcome affected 56.9% of MA vs. 59.7% of FFS patients. Unadjusted hazard ratio (HR) favored MA (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.88–0.91, p<0.0001), but after adjustment, no significant difference was observed (HR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00–1.02, p=0.11).

Conclusions


This study is one of the first comparisons of PAD outcomes by Medicare program. While MA had more Black and dual-enrolled patients, mortality and amputation rates were comparable to FFS.
confex_title: OR1-2 Comparing outcomes of endovascular revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in Medicare Advantage and Medicare Fee-for-service beneficiaries

title: OR1-3 | Impact of GLP-1 Agonist on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Peripheral Artery Disease without Diabetes: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis
full_text:
Background


Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are at heightened risk of adverse cardiovascular events. While glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits in patients with diabetes and cardiovascular disease, their distinct impact on individuals with PAD without diabetes remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate the association between GLP-1RA therapy and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with PAD.

Methods


This retrospective cohort study utilized data from the TrinetX US collaborative network, encompassing adult patients diagnosed with PAD without diabetes between January 2014 and January 2024. Propensity score matching (PSM) analysis compared patients treated with GLP-1RAs for at least one year to those who never received GLP-1RA therapy.

Results


After PSM, the study included 8,956 patients in each cohort, predominantly white females with a mean age of 59.2 years in the GLP-1RA group and 59.7 years in the non-GLP-1RA group. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were similar between the cohorts. The analysis revealed significantly reduced odds of the composite primary outcome of 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) – acute myocardial infarction (AMI), stroke, and all-cause mortality – in the GLP-1RA group (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.337-0.526). Furthermore, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower odds of hospitalization and hypertensive emergency. No significant differences were observed in the odds of requiring amputation and revascularization. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated a significantly higher incidence-free probability for the composite primary outcome in the GLP-1RA group (87.53% vs 79.50%, χ² = 38.189, p < 0.001).

Conclusions


This study suggests that GLP-1RA therapy may confer cardiovascular benefits, including a reduction in 3-point MACE, in patients with PAD independent of diabetes. These findings add to the growing body of evidence supporting the cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1RAs. Further research, including prospective randomized controlled trials, is warranted to validate these findings and establish the implications of GLP-1RA therapy in this patient population.
confex_title: OR1-3 Impact of GLP-1 Agonist on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Peripheral Artery Disease without Diabetes: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis

title: OR1-4 | STRIKE-PE Analysis: Outcomes of Computer Assisted Vacuum Thrombectomy for Treatment of PE in Male vs Female Patients
full_text:
Background


Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening condition with similar prevalence of males and females, yet notable sex disparities exist in outcomes and care. We report sex differences in the safety, effectiveness, and dyspnea in the first 450 patients treated with computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) in STRIKE-PE.

Methods


STRIKE-PE is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter study enrolling up to 1500 patients with acute PE. The primary endpoints are the change in right ventricular/left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio and a composite of major adverse events (MAEs) at 48 hours after CAVT treatment. Secondary endpoints are additional safety endpoints, functional outcomes, and quality of life.

Results


Of the 450 patients, 239 [53.1%] were male and 211 [46.9%] female. Mean age was 61.7±14.1 years for males and 61.7±16.2 years for females. Females had significantly lower hemoglobin and hematocrit levels than males at baseline (both P<.001). Both sexes presented similar classification of PE early mortality risk.

No significant difference in the RV/LV ratio reduction between the sexes. More MAEs occurred in females than in males, specifically major bleeding (2.8% vs 0.4%; P=.038). No significant differences in events that occurred in major bleeding requiring transfusion or device-related transfusion.

Median Borg dyspnea score at rest at baseline was higher for females at 6.0 [IQR 3.0-9.0] than for males at 4.0 [IQR 3.0-7.0] (P=.008). Median Borg dyspnea score improved by decreasing to 0.5 [IQR 0.0-1.0] at discharge and further to 0.0 [IQR 0.0-0.5] at 90 days for both sexes. Females had a greater absolute median change in Borg dyspnea score from baseline to 90 days (−5.5 [−8.0-(−)3.0]; P=.023).

Conclusions


All patients improved in RV/LV ratio at 48 hours and Borg score at discharge. While 90-day Borg score improved in both sexes, females had a greater improvement. Both groups reported low MAEs despite more major bleeding events occurring in females who presented with lower hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. These findings demonstrate that CAVT is a safe and effective treatment for PE in both sexes. The sex-based differences here highlight the importance for further research into underlying factors related to outcomes.
confex_title: OR1-4 STRIKE-PE analysis: Outcomes of computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy for treatment of PE in male vs female patients

title: OR1-5 | Predictors of Clinical Deterioration and Bailout Following Catheter-Directed Intervention for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: Analysis of the PEERLESS Trial
full_text:
Background


The PEERLESS randomized controlled trial (NCT05111613) met its primary endpoint, favoring large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) over catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) in a win ratio analysis. Here, we assess predictors of one component of the win ratio: clinical deterioration and/or escalation to bailout (CD/BO).

Methods


Patients with intermediate-risk PE were randomized 1:1 to LBMT or CDT. Symptom scores (mMRC dyspnea, modified Borg dyspnea at rest, NYHA class) and right ventricular (RV) function on echocardiogram were assessed at the 24-hour visit. CD/BO was assessed through the sooner of discharge or 7 days. Logistic regression was used to identify baseline and 24-hour predictors of CD/BO.

Results


Compared with patients in the CDT arm (n =276), patients in the LBMT arm (n =274) had a significantly lower rate of CD/BO (1.8% vs 5.4%; P =0.038). At the 24-hour visit, the LBMT arm had greater recovery in symptom scores (mMRC dyspnea [P <0.001], modified Borg dyspnea [P =0.026], NYHA class [P =0.002]), respiratory rate (P <0.001), and RV function (P =0.004).

Active cancer, renal dysfunction, and modified Borg score ≥3 at baseline were each associated with higher odds of CD/BO in univariable analysis. When baseline characteristics were assessed with treatment effect in a multivariable model, active cancer (OR 6.5; P =0.001) and treatment with LBMT (OR 0.3; P =0.024) remained significant.

At the 24-hour visit, mMRC score ≥3 (OR 3.0; P =0.037), modified Borg score ≥3 (OR 3.4; P =0.021), NYHA class ≥III (OR 3.3; P =0.021), and moderate or severe RV dysfunction (OR 9.7; P =0.032) were associated with higher odds of CD/BO in individual multivariable models that included active cancer and renal dysfunction.

Conclusions


In PEERLESS, LBMT was associated with a lower rate of CD/BO compared with CDT. When modeled with other baseline predictors, treatment with LBMT remained associated with lower odds of CD/BO. Moderate to severe symptom scores and RV dysfunction at 24 hours were associated with higher odds of CD/BO, suggesting that the faster hemodynamic recovery observed after LBMT is a physiological response underlying the lower rate of CD/BO when compared with CDT.
confex_title: OR1-5 Predictors of Clinical Deterioration and Bailout Following Catheter-Directed Intervention for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: Analysis of the PEERLESS Trial

title: OR1-6 | Persistent Racial Disparities in Access to Care and Outcomes Following Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Between Black and White Medicare Beneficiaries
full_text:
Background




Previous studies have found a higher rate of chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and subsequent complications among Black patients in the US. This study evaluated access to care and outcomes between Black and White patients among a contemporary population of Medicare beneficiaries.

Methods




Medicare beneficiaries who received CLTI endovascular revascularizations from 2016 to 2023 were stratified by race. Kaplan-Meier methods assessed the cumulative incidence of the primary outcome, a composite of major amputation and death. Cox regression adjusted for clinical and sociodemographic/economic factors.

Results




A total of 381,335 patients with CLTI undergoing revascularization were included. After adjustment, Black patients had a significantly higher risk of the primary outcome compared to White patients (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.02; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01, 1.04; p<0.01) driven by a significantly higher risk of major amputation (Figure A). Paradoxically, Black patients had a 10% lower risk of mortality versus White patients (95% CI 0.89, 0.92; p<0.01). Black patients had a higher risk of repeat revascularization compared to White patients (Figure B). Black patients were less likely to see a vascular provider before/after revascularization, but were more likely to have CLTI-related emergency visits and admissions compared to White patients (Figure C).

Conclusions



Black patients revascularized for CLTI were at higher risk of major amputation and lower rates of outpatient vascular care compared to White patients.
confex_title: OR1-6 Persistent Racial Disparities in Access to Care and Outcomes Following Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Between Black and White Medicare Beneficiaries

title: OR1-7 | Association of Guideline-directed Medical Therapy Agents and Rates of Amputation in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure and Chronic Limb Threatening Ischemia
full_text:
Background:


Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation, and concomitant heart failure (HF) further amplifies this risk. However, the impact of individual guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) agents on rates of amputation among CLTI patients with chronic HF remains unclear.

Methods:


We identified adults (≥18 years) with CLTI and chronic HF using the TriNetX database. Amputation risk over 10 years (since inception) was assessed by HF GDMT, including Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitors (ACEi), Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers (ARBs), Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitors (ARNI), Beta-Blockers (BB), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (MRA), and Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors (SGLT2i). We performed 1:1 propensity score matching for patients on GDMT versus those not on GDMT. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess major and minor amputation rates.

Results:


In CLTI patients with HF, use of BBs was associated with higher rates of both major and minor amputations. In contrast, use of ARBs, MRAs, and SGLT2i was associated with lower rates of major amputation. There was no significant association between ACEi or ARNI use and rates of major or minor amputation . For minor amputations, use of MRAs was associated with a reduced rate, while use of other GDMTs had no significant effect.

Conclusions:


BBs are associated with an increased risk of amputations in patients with CLTI and HF, whereas other GDMT may lower the risk. Further investigation is needed into pathophysiologic reasons behind the differential effects of GDMT in this population.
confex_title: OR1-7 Association of guideline-directed medical therapy agents and rates of amputation in patients with chronic heart failure and chronic limb threatening ischemia

title: OR1-8 | Longstanding Disparities in Outcomes Among Medicaid-Enrolled Medicare Beneficiaries with CLTI Undergoing Revascularization (2016–2023)
full_text:
Background


Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) requires timely management to salvage limbs. Socioeconomic disparities, such as Dual Enrollment (DE) in Medicaid, influence healthcare access and outcomes.

Methods



From 2016–2023, 381,335 Medicare beneficiaries undergoing CLTI revascularization were stratified by DE status. The endpoints was a composite of major amputation or death, as well as major amputation, death and repeat revascularization. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methods and multivariable Cox regression. Additional analyses were stratified by COVID periods: pre-COVID (1/16–3/20), during COVID (3/20–12/21), and post-COVID (12/21–12/23).

Results



Overall, 22.9% were DE. These patients were younger, more often female, and had higher comorbidity burdens. After adjustment, DE patients had similar risks of the composite primary endpoint compared to Medicare-only patients (HR 1.00 p=0.98). However, DE patients exhibited higher adjusted risks of major amputation (HR 1.10 p<0.01) and repeat revascularization (HR 1.08 p=0.002). When stratified by COVID periods, DE patients only exhibited an increased risk of the composite outcome during COVID (HR 1.05 p=0.0003) (Figure). However, the adjusted risks of major amputation remained consistently elevated across all periods, and there were greater risks of repeat revascularization across most periods.

Conclusions



DE patients represent a socioeconomically disadvantaged group with greater hazards of major amputation and repeat revascularization. These risks were not exacerbated by the COVID19 pandemic, but remained persistently elevated throughout the last decade.
confex_title: OR1-8 Longstanding Disparities in Outcomes Among Medicaid-Enrolled Medicare Beneficiaries with CLTI Undergoing Revascularization (2016–2023)

title: OR1-9 | Comparative Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Ticagrelor vs. Prasugrel Following PCI of CTO: A Real-World Analysis from the Trinetx Database
full_text:
Background


Ticagrelor and prasugrel are potent P2Y12 inhibitors with established efficacy in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, their comparative long-term outcomes in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) remain understudied.

Methods:
We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing the Trinetx database, encompassing over 100 million patients. Patients undergoing PCI for CTO were identified and divided into two cohorts: ticagrelor and prasugrel. Propensity score matching (PSM) was employed to address potential confounding factors. Primary outcomes included 5-year all-cause mortality and 3-point major adverse cardiac events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke). Secondary outcomes included subsequent ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), in-stent restenosis, and major bleeding. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used for survival analysis.

Results:


Before PSM, the ticagrelor cohort comprised 3,391 patients, while the prasugrel cohort included 976 patients. After PSM, both cohorts were balanced with 974 patients each. Both groups were predominantly composed of white and male patients. 1:1 matching yielded well-balanced cohorts with similar baseline characteristics. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR 1.024, 95% CI 0.766-1.37). Compared to prasugrel, ticagrelor was associated with a significantly higher risk of 3-point MACE (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.098-1.355) and subsequent STEMI (RR 1.243, 95% CI 1.017-1.519). There was also no statistically significant difference in the risk of in-stent restenosis or major bleeding.

Conclusions:


In this real-world analysis, ticagrelor is associated with a higher risk of 3-point MACE and subsequent STEMI compared to prasugrel in patients undergoing PCI for CTO. These findings warrant further prospective studies to help inform optimal antiplatelet therapy strategies in this challenging patient population.
confex_title: OR1-9 Comparative Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Ticagrelor vs. Prasugrel Following PCI of CTO: A Real-World Analysis from the Trinetx Database

title: OR1-10 | Long-Term Outcomes of Rotational versus Orbital Atherectomy in Calcified Coronary Lesions: A Propensity-Matched Analysis
full_text:
Background:
The optimal choice between rotational and orbital atherectomy for calcified coronary lesions remains uncertain, with previous comparisons limited by small samples and brief follow-up.

Methods:
We conducted a propensity-matched analysis using the TriNetX Analytics Network database comparing rotational and orbital atherectomy procedures (2015-2023). Primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), recurrent myocardial infarction, angina, stroke, and post-procedural cardiac arrest.

Results:
Among 1,084 matched pairs followed for a median of 639.5 days, rotational atherectomy showed lower all-cause mortality (22.7% vs 30.2%; hazard ratio[HR], 0.74; 95%CI, 0.63-0.88; P<0.001) and MACCE (24.0% vs 38.1%; HR, 0.59; 95%CI, 0.43-0.80; P=0.001). While recurrent myocardial infarction rates were similar (14.8% vs 16.5%; HR, 0.93; P=0.661), angina occurred less frequently with rotational atherectomy (10.2% vs 17.6%; risk ratio, 0.58; P<0.001). Stroke rates (4.0% vs 4.9%) and post-procedural cardiac arrest (0.9% both groups) were comparable. After adjustment, rotational atherectomy maintained lower mortality (adjusted HR, 0.79; 95%CI, 0.71-0.88; P<0.001) and MACCE (adjusted HR, 0.69; 95%CI, 0.64-0.74; P<0.001).

Conclusions:
In this large propensity-matched analysis, rotational atherectomy demonstrated significantly lower risks of mortality and adverse cardiovascular events compared to orbital atherectomy over long-term follow-up, suggesting it may be preferred for complex calcified coronary lesions.
confex_title: OR1-10 Long-Term Outcomes of Rotational versus Orbital Atherectomy in Calcified Coronary Lesions: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

title: OR1-11 | Comparative Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention vs. Medical Management in Chronic Coronary Occlusion: A Propensity-Matched Analysis
full_text:
Background


The management of chronic coronary occlusion (CCO) through percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) versus medical management remains a topic of clinical debate. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of PCI and medical management cohorts, focusing on cardiovascular mortality, MACE, and symptoms over a 3-month and 1 year follow-up period.

Methods


A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using TriNetX database, including 11,582 patients in the PCI group and 25,058 patients in the medical management group before matching. After propensity score matching, 10,341 patients were included in each cohort.

Results


At 3 months, all cause mortality was higher in the PCI cohort (5.493%) compared to the medical management cohort (4.845%), with a risk difference of 0.648% (p = 0.0354), RR of 1.134 (95% CI: 1.009–1.274). All MACEs (Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events) occurred more frequently in the PCI cohort (79.91%) than in the medical management cohort (72.54%), with a significant risk difference of 7.378% (p < 0.0001), RR of 1.102 (95% CI: 1.085–1.119). Dyspnea rates were similar, occurring in 14.93% of the PCI cohort and 15.11% of the medical group, with a non-significant risk difference of -0.174% (p = 0.7261) and RR of 0.988 (95% CI: 0.926–1.055). At one year,cardiovascular mortality was still higher in the PCI group (8.44%) compared to medical management (7.25%), with a risk difference of 1.19% (p = 0.03) and a risk ratio of 1.165. All MACEs were significantly higher in the PCI cohort (85.51% vs. 76.17%), with a risk difference of 9.34% (p < 0.0001), a risk ratio of 1.123.

Conclusions


PCI in chronic coronary occlusion is linked to higher rate of all cause mortality and risks of long-term MACEs compared to medical management. These findings emphasize the importance of patient selection and risk stratification to balance benefits and risks of PCI effectively.
confex_title: OR1-11 Comparative Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention vs. Medical Management in Chronic Coronary Occlusion: A Propensity-Matched Analysis

title: OR1-12 | Drug-Coated Versus Uncoated Balloon for Side Branch in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions
full_text:
Background:
Bifurcation lesions pose unique challenges during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and are associated with suboptimal outcomes. The standard approach involves provisional stenting of the main branch (MB) with balloon angioplasty (BA) for compromised side branches (SB). It remains unclear whether drug-coated balloons or plain balloon angioplasty pose a better strategy to treat SB in bifurcation lesions.

Methods:
MEDLINE, Cochrane, and EMBASE databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DCB and BA for treating bifurcation lesions. Outcomes included SB late lumen loss (LLL), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and target lesion revascularization (TLR).

Results:
Five RCTs were included encompassing 1,255 patients, of which 628/50.4underwent DCB angioplasty, 477/ 38% were male. DCB significantly reduced MI risk (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.39–0.74; P=0.0001) (Figure1A). DCB use resulted in similar LLL in the SB compared with BA (MD: -0.12 mm; 95% CI: -0.24 to 0.01; P=0.07). No significant differences were observed in TLR (RR: 1.19; 95% CI: 0.45–3.14; P=0.72), TVR (RR: 1.24; 95% CI: 0.26–5.87; P=0.78), MACE (RR: 0.70; 95% CI: 0.48–1.02; P=0.07) (Figure 1B), and all-cause mortality (RR: 2.35; 95% CI: 0.61-9.00; P=0.21).

Conclusions:
In this meta-analysis of RCTs, DCB significantly reduced MI without affecting LLL, TLR, or TVR, MACE, and all-cause mortality compared with BA in the SB of bifurcation lesions.
confex_title: Drug-Coated Balloons vs. Plain Balloon Angioplasty for Side Branch Management in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
